headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 20 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: The final mountain showdown! On the eve of the grand finale in Granada, the peloton face emblematic summits such as the Puerto de El Purche en route to an unprecedented finish. The stage is packed with climbing: 5 categorised ascents (53 KOM points) and almost 5,000 metres of elevation gain between La Calahorra and Collado del Alguacil (186.8 km). The neutral start is set at 12:30, the start proper at 12:36 after a 1.8 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Collado del Alguacil makes its La Vuelta debut
Welcome (back) to Granada
subtext: La Vuelta 26 returns to the province of Granada (previously home to stage 13) for the final week-end. For the first time in the race history, all the Andalusian provinces hosted at least one stage in its entirety: Almeria (stage 12), Jaen (stage 14), Cordoba (15), Huelva (16), Seville (17), Cadiz (18), and Malaga (19). Both La Calahorra and Collado del Alguacil make their debuts as La Vuelta stage towns. The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Alguacil (20).

headline: A familiar area, especially for Carlos Rodriguez
subtext: Most riders are familiar with the area, either thanks to the many races organised around Granada, or from the training camps teams and riders are used to hold in the Sierra Nevada. Carlos Rodriguez (Netcompany Ineos) is the local rider of the day, hailing from Almuñecar in the province of Granada. His hometown hosted the start of stage 13 a week ago.

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with an 1.8 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Despite the attacks launched by Richard Carrapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) and Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), the top GC contenders finished together yesterday at Peñas Blancas. Enric Mas (Movistar), the overall leader since stage 8, enters the final week-end with a lead of 1’37’’ over Roglic. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) follows with a gap of 3’01’’, and Carapaz trails by 5’17’’. Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) completes the top 5, 6’03’’ behind Mas.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Victory is in sight for Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), who still leads the points standings with 306 points, 69 more than his British teammate Matthew Brennan. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) follows with 171 points. A rider can grab a maximum of 90 points in the final two stages, including 40 today (20 at the finish, 20 at the intermediate sprint). That means Brennan is (barring significant incidents) the last rider still in a position to contest the green jersey, but Van Aert could seal the deal today, and even already at the intermediate sprint.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: With another breakaway in the mountains, and another top 3 result at a summit finish, Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) extended his lead in the mountains standings: 78 points against 40 for Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike). Also at the front, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) is back to third place with 29 points. Today’s mountain showdown offers up to 53 points, including 20 at the finish at Collado del Alguacil (Cima Alberto Fernandez).

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) “felt good” in yesterday’s finale and he gained a handful of seconds on Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious), now trailing by 1’03’’. Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) is still third in the young riders standings, 13’14’’ behind the Briton.

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Eddie Dunbar (1st), Thomas Gloag (3rd) and Marcel Camprubi (5th) dominating the climb up Peñas Blancas, Pinarello Q36.5 had the strongest collective performance yesterday. Decathlon CMA CGM still lead the overall team standings with a gap of 58’06’’ to XDS Astana and 1h09’36’’ to Groupama-FDJ United.

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) will race with a distinctive bib again as he was named the most combative rider on his way to a spectacular stage win at Peñas Blancas.

headline: Stage 20 is ON!
subtext: There are 145 starters.

headline: Van Aert immediately sets off
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) initiates the battle for the breakaway with Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG).

headline: Van Aert and Oliveira keep pushing
subtext: The duo are half a minute ahead of the bunch after 13 kilometres.

headline: Van Aert to (all but) secure the green jersey?
subtext: The Belgian powerhouse leads the points standings with a gap of 67 points to Brennan. There are 90 points still up for grabs on the road of La Vuelta 26, and there will be 70 after today's intermediate sprint (Güejar Sierra, km 144.0). So if Van Aert scores three more points than Brennan there, he will be mathematically out of reach. Otherwise, the battle should be settled at the finish up Collado del Alguacil.

headline: Splits in the bunch
subtext: The first bunch trail by 30'', the second by 50. They're at km 18.

headline: Mas is caught behind
subtext: His Movistar teammates in the first peloton drop back to drive the chase for the wearer of La Roja.

headline: The bunches get back together
subtext: Meanwhile, there's a group of chasers featuring six Uno-X Mobility riders 15 seconds behind the leading duo, who have covered 25 kilometres.

headline: Uno-X Mobility vs Movistar
subtext: The Scandinavian team work hard at the front of the race, but Enric Mas's teammates also set a strong pace in the peloton. The gap at km 32: 50 seconds.

headline: Movistar on the counter-attack
subtext: Raul Garcia Pierna and Ivan Romeo (Movistar) set off from the bunch with Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and James Shaw (EF Education-EasyPost). At km 35, they are 25 seconds behind the 14 leaders.

headline: The battle goes on after almost 40 kilometres of hard racing
subtext: The fourteen leaders don't look behind. The four chasers were joined by a fez dozens more, but Enric Mas (Movistar) and his teammates reacted to regroup the bunch.

headline: Crash in the first positions of the peloton
subtext: Matthew Riccitello (Decathlon CMA CGM) rapidly got back up but Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL) was in much more pain.

headline: Riccitello abandons after his crash
subtext: Meanwhile, the battle goes on with a group of 27 chasers between the 14 leaders and the peloton (+50'').

subtext: The leaders make their way up the Puerto de Los Blancares, a classic ascent for events in the area. The first chasers trail by 35 seconds. More attackers set off from the bunch to make the jump to the chasers.

headline: 49.2 km in the first hour
subtext: That's a brutal pace on rolling terrain... And the battle goes on!

headline: Miquel leads the way to the first summit
subtext: The Spaniard defends Buitrago's polka-dot jersey against Van Aert. The chase group, with the likes of Dunbar, JF Rodriguez and Vansevenant, trail by 1 minute. The peloton are 1 minute further behind.

headline: The gaps increase on the valley
subtext: The 14 leaders have covered 81 km. The chasers trail by 3'10''. The peloton are 8'25'' behind.

headline: Carapaz, inspired again by the Puerto de El Purche?
subtext: Collado del Alguacil is in the municipality of Güejar Sierra, like Alto de Hazallanas. This climb made its debut in La Vuelta 13 (Chris Horner won the stage and took La Roja form Vincenzo Nibali) and was at the heart of stage 9 in La Vuelta 24, with two ascents up Alto de Hazallanas before finishing in Granada. Part of the breakaway, Adam Yates attacked on these slopes, and covered the last 57 kilometres alone to take the win. Richard Carapaz was 2nd that day as he attacked the GC group up the Puerto de El Purche, with 90 kilometres remaining. This daring move allowed him to gain two minutes on his GC rivals, including Primoz Roglic, the final winner of this edition.

headline: The most beautiful sport in the world
Onto the Puerto de El Purche
subtext: Uno-X Mobility drive the breakaway into the final 100 kilometres as they begin the first ascent of the Puerto de El Purche (8.2 km at 8.2%). Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) is dropped early on the climb.

headline: The chasers begin the ascent
subtext: They trail by three and a half minutes at the bottom. Meanwhile, the gap to the peloton increases to 10'30''.

headline: Martin-Guyonnet enters the virtual GC top 10
subtext: There is now a gap of 8 minutes between the chasers and the peloton. At the start of the stage, Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United) was 7'52'' behind Harold Tejada (XDS Astana), 10th in the overall standings. He needs 9'13'' to catch Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek).

headline: Martin-Guyonnet: "I’m expecting major race developments quite early on"
subtext: Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United): “No, I don’t know the Sierra Nevada as well as I know Normandy! I know Normandy very well. I know the Sierra Nevada well, as do most of the riders in the peloton, having done training camps there. I know what to expect. I know it’s going to be a really tough stage, undoubtedly the queen stage of this Vuelta, with climbs that aren’t necessarily very long but are really steep. Ultimately, it’s the only stage, so to speak, in these three weeks where there could be moves very early on for the favourites, because there are steep climbs with little recovery, so I’m expecting major race developments quite early on. [Clément Berthet] is showing that he’s getting better and better with each passing day, holding on firmly to his seventh place. He’s had a difficult season, but his luck is turning, and I’m going to try to support him on this big day.”

headline: Sepp Kuss attacks from the bunch
subtext: The American climber has a massive gap to close. But he's likely to receive support from teammates who can drop from the chasing group. Armirail, Brennan, Kruijswijk and Nordhagen are all there.

headline: The leaders face the final 3 km of ascent
subtext: Meanwhile, Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) has opened a 25'' gap to the bunch.

headline: Carapaz attacks with 99 km to go
subtext: Decathlon CMA CGM take over the pace-setting in the bunch.

headline: Carapaz joins Kuss
subtext: They are 35 seconds ahead of the bunch. Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek) struggles.

headline: Van Aert leads the way to the summit; 11 riders in the GC group
subtext: Bisiaux and Scotsom set the pace for Gall. Tejada and Cr. Rodriguez are both there. Onley also has a teammate: Haig. The others are alone: Mas, Roglic, Omrzel, and Berthet.

headline: Gall closes the gap at the summit
subtext: Roglic and Mas followed the Austrian climber while Onley and the others lost a few metres.

headline: Carapaz has 2 teammates with him now
subtext: Albanese and Mackellar have dropped back to the GC group. Brennan is also here to help Kuss. The Onley group are 45 seconds behind.

headline: Back on the slopes of El Purche
subtext: Uno-X Mobility continue setting a strong pace at the front as they face for the second time the 8.2-km climb (average gradient: 8.2%; max: 18%).

subtext: Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Oscar Chamberlain (Decathlon CMA CGM), Pau Miquel (Bahrain Victorious) and Louis Rouland (Cofidis) are here with Simon Dalby, Tobias Johannessen, Andreas Kron and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility).

subtext: Mackellar now sets the pace, followed by Carapaz, Gall, Mas, Roglic, Kruijswijk, Kuss, and Herrada.

headline: 4 chasers 2'30'' behind the leaders
subtext: This group is made of Walter Calzoni (Pinarello Q36.5), Lucas Hamilton (Netcompany Ineos), Mikel Landa (Soudal Quick-Step), and Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma).

headline: The gap from the Mas group to the Onley group has significantly increased
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) and his companions are three and a half minutes behind Enric Mas (Movistar).

headline: Kuss attacks the GC group
subtext: The American is around 5 kilometres from the summit. De Pestel sets the pace in the group.

headline: Calzoni and Landa move closer to the leaders
subtext: With 3 kilometres to the summit, they are 1'10'' behind the front of the race. Meanwhile, Kuss has opened a gap of 25 seconds to the GC group.

headline: The leaders face the final kilometre up El Purche

subtext: The Belgian is now 16 points behind Buitrago. There are 10 points for the first rider at Puerto de El Duque, and 20 for the winner of the stage.

subtext: Gall immediately reacts, followed by Mas and Roglic.

headline: Landa joins the leading group

subtext: 1. Van Aert, 10 pts 2. Miquel, 6 pts 3. Leknessund, 4 pts 4. Chamberlain, 2 pts 5. Kron, 1 pt

headline: Carapaz is caught by Gall, Mas and Roglic
subtext: They are 7'20'' behind the leaders, and 50'' behind Kuss.

headline: 50 kilometres to go
subtext: The leaders are headed to the intermediate sprint. If Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) scores points there, he will be mathematically out of reach from anyone.

headline: Richard Carapaz accelerates on the downhill
subtext: The GC contenders are 7'30'' behind the leaders. Oscar Chamberlain is dropped from the breakaway. Is he waiting for Felix Gall?

headline: Kuss is 2 minutes ahead of the Mas group
subtext: He is 6 minutes behind the leaders.

headline: 45 kilometres to go
subtext: Van Aert is about to seal the deal for the green jersey at the intermediate sprint. Debruyne is 40'' behind the leaders. Then, the chasing group trail by 1'25''. In the GC group, Garcia Pierna sets the pace for Mas two minutes behind Kuss and 8 minutes behind the leaders.

headline: Van Aert (all but) secures the green jersey
subtext: As the Belgian superstar goes first at the intermediate sprint, he only needs to finish the race without incidents to win the points standings tomorrow in Granada.

headline: Leknessund is spent
subtext: Now Kron sets the pace, followed by Dalby and Johannessen. Chamberlain returns to the front group.

headline: The penultimate climb of the day: Puerto de El Duque
subtext: Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) is just behind the leaders at the bottom of the 7.4 km ascent at 8.3 %. Puerto de El Duque makes its debut in La Vuelta to replace the ascent of Alto de Hazallanas after landslides caused by the severe weather that hit the area last February have made it impossible for the race to use the originally planned route . The new climb shares its final section with the ascent initially planned.

headline: Debruyne accelerates with 38 km to go
subtext: The Belgian youngster is followed by Johannessen and Landa.

headline: Roglic sets the pace in the GC group
subtext: He's dollowed by Mas, Gall, Carapaz, Rodriguez and Gogl.

subtext: Carapaz is in second position, followed by Gall, Mas, and Roglic.

subtext: +1'35'' Chaser group +5' Kuss +8' Mas group

headline: Carapaz has another go

headline: Landa leads the way to the summit

subtext: The leaders are 28 kilometres from the finish. Miquel trails by 30 seconds.

headline: Carapaz tries again and again
subtext: But he is not finding an opening.

headline: 20 kilometres to go for the leading trio
subtext: The final ascent begins with 8.3 km to go.

headline: Collado del Alguacil, a new summit in professional cycling
subtext: The Collado del Alguacil climb is an unprecedented climb in the world of professional cycling that was, according to Luis Angel Maté’s account, discovered by the late Xavi Tondo. Hailing from Tarragona (Catalonia), Tondo used to train in Sierra Nevada with his coach Francis Cabello (11 participations in La Vuelta between 1990 and 2004, 1 stage win in the Tour de France) and was keen to explore new roads, which led him to the heights of Collado del Alguacil. He finished 5th in La Vuelta 10, and passed away in May 2011 in a tragic accident while he was getting ready to train in the mountains of Granada.

subtext: The American climber is currently riding 5'25'' ahead of the Mas group. He started the day 5'47'' behind Carapaz on GC.

headline: The final climb to make the decision!
subtext: The road rises brutally: 8.3 km at 9.8 %, with gradients up to 22%.

headline: The Kuss group are 3 minutes behind the leaders
subtext: Van Aert sets the pace at the bottom of the climb, followed by Nordhagen, Kuss, Calzoni, Fortunato, Berrade and Widar.

subtext: Debruyne is the first to fade, and then Johannessen is dropped with 7 km to go.

headline: Van Aert is spent
subtext: The Belgian superstar all but secures the green jersey, but Buitrago is set to keep the polka dot jersey. Now Nordhagen sets the pace 3 minutes behind Landa.

headline: Landa vs Johannessen
subtext: The Spaniard leads by 23 seconds as he tackles the final 4 kilometres. Debruyne trails by 55''. The Kuss group are 5 km from the summit.

headline: Landa is closing in
subtext: The Spanish veteran is 2 km from the summit. He's headed for his second La Vuelta stage win, eleven years after his victory in Andorra!

headline: Mas is in control

headline: Gall attacks

headline: Last kilometre for Landa
subtext: The Basque icon is increasing his lead.

headline: Gall drops Mas
subtext: The Spanish wearrer of La Roja loses a few metres. Roglic is 25 seconds behind.

headline: Mikel Landa wins stage 20 of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: The Spanish climber can't believe it. What an emotional resurrection!

subtext: +10'' Mas +40'' Roglic +1'10'' Carapaz
